title: OpenAI Builds a Central Control Room: Real-Time Tracking of Model Workloads Ensures Second-Level Shutdown Within 35 Seconds After Anomaly Intervention

content_html:
As the scale and reasoning capabilities of frontier AI models continue to surge, the industry has imposed unprecedented and stringent requirements on safety monitoring and emergency shutdown mechanisms for high-risk models during operation. Recently, leading AI company OpenAI officially announced that it has built a new centralized research workload management and control system—Control Room. The system's core mission is to track model workloads in research infrastructure in real time and, upon detecting potential safety or security concerns, shut down related work at extremely high speed.

Core Functions and Operating Mechanism: Deep Coordination with the Misalignment Monitoring System

As an important part of OpenAI's overall safety training and deployment plan for frontier models, Control Room covers all research inference workloads.

In the actual operating architecture, this control room does not operate in isolation; instead, it maintains seamless coordination with an advanced Misalignment Monitoring System. Once the monitoring system detects abnormal deviations, safety risks, or security concerns in model operation, the control room responds quickly. Official data shows that after management or the system formally decides to intervene to pause or stop a specific task, Control Room can completely terminate the relevant model's continued output within 35 seconds, thereby building a solid safety defense line for the technical team at critical moments.
